_readme: Seed evaluation set. THIS IS A STARTING POINT, NOT A FINISHED BENCHMARK. It currently covers one document (a resume PDF) because that's what's indexed. Before trusting any number this harness reports: (1) verify expected_keywords actually reflect a correct answer by re-reading the source document, (2) expand to 5-10 documents of different types (paper, contract/report, slides, spreadsheet) per the improvement plan, (3) aim for 50+ questions total. Each item's category is 'factual' (answerable from the indexed document(s)) or 'unanswerable' (deliberately out of scope, to test the refusal path).

items.question: What degree is this person pursuing and at which institute?
What internship did this person do at Authenta.ai?
What did this person do during their internship at Inadev Pvt. Ltd.?
What programming languages are listed under technical skills?
What machine learning frameworks or libraries does this person know?
What is the QuantEdge Investment Advisor project about?
What certifications does this person have?
What achievements or awards are listed?
What position of responsibility did this person hold in the Coding Ninjas Club?
What database technologies are mentioned in the skills section?
What cloud or DevOps tools does this person list?
What is the capital of France?
items.notes: Not in the document at all -- must trigger the refusal path, not a hallucinated fact.

items.question: What was this person's salary at their internship?
items.notes: Plausible-sounding but not present in a resume -- checks the system doesn't invent numbers.

items.question: Summarize this person's PhD thesis.
items.notes: Presupposes something false (a PhD thesis) -- checks the system doesn't play along with a false premise.
